root_idea.summary: The root develops several lexical branches: harmful fouling or affliction, sound, elevation, and the handling or working of something. The Quranic forms chiefly reflect harmful consequence and the approach of a needy petitioner.
root_idea.development: The primary semantic orientation links mange, dirt, and harmful contamination with what befalls or burdens someone; related branches extend to sounds, attachment or approach, high points, and vigorous treatment of a difficult object.

qac_form_accounting.reason: A distinct Quranic active-participial noun meaning one who approaches seeking bounty.
A distinct Quranic noun denoting harm or adverse consequence.

senses.definition: One who comes to another seeking favor or bounty; especially a needy petitioner.
senses.usage_conditions: The approach may involve an explicit request or merely presenting oneself before the person whose bounty is sought. In the Quranic construction, the word is associated with the needy who approach for provision.

senses.definition: Harm, injury, or an adverse consequence.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic usage, it denotes harm that may result from an action or situation, including an unintended harmful consequence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels: to become affected with mange, scab, or a related purulent skin eruption.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The disease may appear as dispersed pustules, discharge, or loss of fur; the same verb is also used of the disease attacking the body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mange, scab, or a purulent skin disease affecting animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Descriptions include pustules on young camels and a disease causing the fur to fall away so that the skin shows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dung or defecate; to manure land; or to befoul something with dung.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intransitive use may be said of a bird; transitive uses concern land or an object defiled with dung.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sully or bespatter someone with evil; to accuse, disgrace, wrong, revile, or injuriously deprive him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is also used of bringing an abominable charge against a person or group, applying a disgraceful nickname, or doing what another dislikes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For an unwelcome or distressing thing to befall someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This use is explained as equivalent to a thing coming upon or overtaking him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To alight at someone's abode as a visitor or guest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a conventional visiting construction distinct from approaching someone to seek bounty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a male ostrich: to cry or utter a call.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The corresponding call of the female ostrich is distinguished in the lexical description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a house to contain dung or human ordure, especially in abundance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes a place in which such filth is present.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To awaken from sleep during the night with speech, a sound, or a cry, and remain restless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may include turning over in bed while speaking or making a sound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For mange or scab to appear and spread among a group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject is the disease, and the object is the group among whom it spreads.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vice, fault, evil, or mischief; something morally foul or harmful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This figurative noun extends the language of physical affliction and contamination to moral conduct and its effects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Madness or a condition understood as resulting from diabolical possession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It occurs in the expression بِهِ عُرَّةٌ, ‘there is madness in him.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dung or ordure, including animal dung and human excrement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can refer to dung of birds, camels, sheep, goats, and other animals, as well as human ordure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dirt or filth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the general physical-filth use, distinct from the more specific use for dung.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Moral filth, a disgrace, vice, fault, or abominable act that exposes someone to blame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: As an epithet of a person, it may describe someone dirty, disgraced, or a source of shame to his people; it can also denote an evil act done to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Manginess or scabbiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Some authorities use it for the disease itself, while others use it for the condition of being mangy or scabby.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sweet-scented plant with intensely yellow blossoms, identified with a kind of ox-eye or wild narcissus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun has a singulative form in ـة and is also used for related plant identifications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Retaliation by killing, wounding, or mutilation; also the thing slain in retaliation for another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is used in the sense of legal or customary equivalence and retaliation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stranger or outsider among a people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can describe one who is attached to or present among people without belonging to them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large evergreen mountain tree, identified variously with cypress, juniper, or a related tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The botanical identifications vary among authorities; the word is also treated as a plant name rather than a productive semantic derivative.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An imitative representation of the rustling or hissing sound of wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same sound-naming branch is extended to the call of the male ostrich.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A children's calling game in which a child raises his voice so that other children come out to him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is treated as an imitation of a cry or calling sound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affected with mange or scab; said of a camel and, in one usage, of a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective denotes the bearer of the disease rather than the disease itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Worse or more evil than another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This comparative figurative use is explicitly associated with the synonymous pairing of evil terms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place containing mange or scab.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is identified as the primary concrete signification of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The region of the sky beyond the Milky Way toward the North Pole; in some accounts, a star or asterism below the Milky Way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by comparison of the numerous stars with scabs on a body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sin, crime, offense, cause of disgrace or reviling, foul act, or source of vexation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This figurative branch describes conduct or a circumstance that brings blame, grief, annoyance, or moral reproach.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unauthorized harm or depredation inflicted by an army on people among whom it passes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may refer to fighting or killing without the commander's permission, taking produce, oppressing inhabitants, or violating their persons and property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A debt, fine, or mulct that one is obliged to pay, including a fine for homicide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also denote an unwelcome financial liability associated with a killing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dunged or treated with عُرَّة; said of a palm tree or land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a passive agricultural use referring to the application of dung or ordure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sullied or bespattered with evil; wronged, reviled, or deprived of property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This passive-personal use belongs to the figurative branch of being charged with or afflicted by evil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A visiting guest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical usage of the active participle distinct from the Quranic use of one approaching to seek bounty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The top, highest part, or crest of something; specifically the tip of a hump, and by extension a fat or distinguished person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These elevated or status-related uses are reported as a separate Classical branch of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To work at or manipulate something rapidly, especially something difficult to remove or handle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Examples include working meat away from a bone or working at the neck of a bottle to extract it.

cautions: مُعْتَرّ is Quranically explained as one who approaches seeking bounty, with the Classical discussion also recording the related readings ‘poor person’ and ‘visiting guest’; these are kept distinct where the evidence distinguishes them.
The Lane citation attached to مُعْتَرّ uses an abbreviated historical Quran reference; the modern example location here is taken from QAC, not reconstructed from the Lane notation.
The face-changing meaning under مَعَرَّة is left unassigned because the source itself questions whether it belongs to عرر or to تَمَعَّرَ.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:Err:2623:g1:sub5 reports changing facial color from anger but explicitly says the form may derive from تَمَعَّرَ rather than عرر, so it cannot be assigned confidently to this root.
